record.paper_title: Toward epidemic thresholds on temporal networks: a review and open questions
record.context_brief: Applying threshold theory with incomplete data
record.original_question: Epidemic-threshold theory for temporal networks is usually developed under the unrealistic assumption that the full sequence of contact networks is observed. In practical risk assessment, one may only have partial samples or coarse observations of the evolving network. How can epidemic-threshold methods be applied under incomplete observation, with quantified uncertainty from sampling, and what kinds of data are sufficient for reliable prediction in different epidemiological settings?

evidence.quote: While significant advances have been made in the theory of estimating epidemic thresholds on temporal networks, there has been comparatively little progress in understanding how to apply this theory. One key application is that of risk assessment in case of real-world infectious diseases and outbreaks. To date, this has largely been an unexplored area of research.
In most of the current literature on epidemic thresholds, the underlying contact network is assumed to be fully known and observed.
Understanding what kind of data is needed in which epidemiological context is an important direction of future research.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathcal{G} = (G_t)_{t \in [0,T]}$ be a temporal contact network on a fixed vertex set $V$ of $n$ individuals, where each $G_t = (V, E_t)$ is a (possibly weighted) graph describing the contacts active at time $t$. Consider an SIS or SIR compartmental epidemic model on $\mathcal{G}$ with per-contact infection rate $\beta$ and recovery rate $\mu$, and let $\tau_c(\mathcal{G})$ denote the epidemic threshold of the model on $\mathcal{G}$, defined (e.g., via the dominant eigenvalue of the appropriate infection-propagation operator built from $(G_t)$) as the critical value of $\beta/\mu$ separating the regime in which an initial infection dies out almost surely from the regime in which it persists/spreads with positive probability as $n \to \infty$.

Standard threshold theory assumes that the entire trajectory $(G_t)_{t \in [0,T]}$ is observed. Suppose instead that one only has access to a partial observation $\mathcal{O}$ of $\mathcal{G}$, formalized as one of the following:
(i) a temporal subsample: $G_t$ is observed only for $t$ in a random or deterministic subset $S \subseteq [0,T]$;
(ii) a vertex/edge subsample: at each observed time, only the induced subgraph on a random subset $V' \subseteq V$, or a Bernoulli-sampled subset of edges, is recorded;
(iii) a coarse aggregation: only time-aggregated graphs $\bar G_k = \bigcup_{t \in I_k} G_t$ over a partition $\{I_k\}$ of $[0,T]$ are observed.

Develop a methodology that, given $\mathcal{O}$, produces an estimator $\hat\tau_c(\mathcal{O})$ of $\tau_c(\mathcal{G})$ together with a quantitative uncertainty bound, i.e., explicit nonasymptotic or asymptotic confidence intervals
$$\Pr\big(|\hat\tau_c(\mathcal{O}) - \tau_c(\mathcal{G})| \leq \varepsilon(\mathcal{O})\big) \geq 1 - \delta,$$
where $\varepsilon(\mathcal{O})$ depends explicitly on the sampling design and intensity. Furthermore, characterize, for each epidemiological regime (e.g., short-timescale outbreaks vs. endemic dynamics; sparse vs. dense contact networks; SIS vs. SIR), the minimal class of partial observations $\mathcal{O}$ that is sufficient to guarantee a prescribed accuracy $\varepsilon$ with confidence $1-\delta$ in the threshold estimate.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an open research direction: applying epidemic-threshold theory on temporal networks under incomplete/sampled observations with quantified uncertainty. While there is ongoing work on network sampling, threshold estimation from temporal data, and uncertainty quantification in epidemic models, no general framework that solves the problem across observation regimes and epidemiological settings has been established. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Toward epidemic thresholds on temporal networks: a review and open questions
status_evidence.snippet: Review identifying applications of epidemic-threshold theory under incomplete observation as a largely unexplored area.
status_evidence.claim: The problem of applying threshold theory with partial/sampled temporal-network data and quantified uncertainty is identified as open.
